She went inside and came back with the flask from the lab windowsill, dust still on its shoulders. Her grandmother had carried wine like it to night shifts. Her mother had. Eteri had carried this one through a whole winter and a year before it. She worked the stopper loose and poured into two chipped tea cups and handed him one.

"For luck?" Bohdan said.

"For after luck," she said, and drank. It was cold and a little sour and tasted of her grandmother's kitchen. Bohdan drank his in one swallow, the way his father must have on the tractor, and wiped his stubble with the back of his hand.

The ramp pinched at the top into one last tight mud slot. Hollis's voice came down through it, not on the radio but out loud, bellowing at them to clip in, and the yellow rope went taut. Up top the surface team had it, a line of volunteers in the rain.

Jolene went first, because Darlene told her to, and hands took her out of the slot. Then Priya, the surface team pulling the rope steady while Darlene pushed from below and talked her through every scrape. Behind them the throat of the lower passage filled and roared, and the pool swallowed the ledge where they had stood ten minutes before.

Darlene went last. She squeezed through with her shoulders scraping, thinking of all the times she had told her seventh graders to keep three points of contact.
